en.bestFor: Turning an FAQ, article or explainer topic into a two-character conversation for Reels, Shorts, onboarding or support content, where viewers learn by overhearing.
en.structure: Each clip runs 3–8 seconds and carries one question, one answer, or a quick question with its reply: about 1–2 clips for micro (one exchange), 2–4 for 15–20s, 4–6 for 30–45s, and 7–10 for 50–60s (up to five exchanges).
en.hook: The asker kicks off with the most surprising or relatable question while already moving or holding the object in question — no greetings or introductions.
en.arc: A ladder of questions that keeps getting sharper ("but what if…", "then why…"); each answer reveals one idea and sets up the next question. The biggest "aha" lands in the last third, followed by a satisfied reaction and one short closing line.
en.narrator: No narrator. You must pick exactly 2 characters: an asker who stands in for the viewer and a calm, knowledgeable answerer. Each keeps a distinct voice that stays the same all the way through.
en.visual: Look and palette come from the chosen visual style. The two characters keep fixed sides for the whole video; props or simple diagrams between them illustrate each answer, and the asker visibly reacts every time.
en.audio: No background music — reaction and prop sound effects only, with a lift at the "aha" moment. Dialogue is audio only, never shown as subtitles or speech bubbles.
en.rules: Exactly two character images are required. Answers only use facts from your source; questions the source can't answer are dropped. The characters never swap sides and no third person appears.
